headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Botpress can ingest files and Great Expectations writes validation artifacts, creating a default workspace bridge with limited but real misuse potential.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while Great Expectations reads and writes files such as validation results and documentation. If Botpress ingests those outputs as trusted text, prompt injection can cross the shared file bridge. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Botpress reads Great Expectations output files as instructions or context
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Prefix all Great Expectations outputs with machine-only markers
Require manual review before Botpress consumes any validation report
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into Botpress prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations explicitly touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, and Botpress has no documented network egress but also no documented workspace isolation. A shared filesystem can expose sensitive validation artifacts to Botpress outputs or logs. The blast radius is more than one document because validation results often summarize multiple datasets, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or workspace
IF validation results contain sensitive dataset names or findings
mitigations: Store validation outputs in a separate folder with restricted permissions
Redact sensitive fields before Botpress can read reports
Turn off any Botpress feature that auto-loads local files
Review logs for accidental inclusion of validation artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can install packages, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git, database, or OAuth write scopes, and both have network egress set to none. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible overlap is package installation in a shared environment, which is usually manageable and has limited blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same Python or node environment
IF package installation targets the same shared interpreter or site-packages
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments
Pin package versions for both agents
Install dependencies during a maintenance window
Avoid concurrent package installs in the same environment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, and Botpress is a conversational agent that can summarize or act on text. If Botpress forwards validation findings without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect support guidance or operational decisions. The pairwise interaction is inferred from documented roles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress uses Great Expectations validation results as source-of-truth
IF no human or rule-based verification step exists before Botpress acts
mitigations: Require a human review step before actioning validation results
Have Botpress cite the original data source, not only the report
Add a checksum or schema check on validation outputs
Limit Botpress to summarizing, not deciding, on GE findings

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, but neither profile shows regulated data handling, residency constraints, or retention policies. Botpress also has no declared sensitive-data classes. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is limited to documentation and logging hygiene rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Great Expectations outputs
IF Botpress logs or stores those outputs beyond the intended retention period
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in validation reports
Set a short log-retention window
Document which datasets may flow through each agent
Review outputs for accidental inclusion of personal data
